abstract: Which automorphisms can a directed strongly regular graph with the unresolved parameters $(108,15,11,2,2)$ admit? We prove that every automorphism of order three is fixed-point-free and that no automorphism has prime order at least five. Consequently the full automorphism group has order $2^a3^b$ with $b\leq3$, and every $3$-subgroup acts semiregularly. The conclusions also hold for the complementary parameters $(108,92,88,78,80)$. The proof starts from the fact that two distinct fixed vertices have exactly two directed two-walks between them, so an odd-prime-order automorphism fixes every intermediate vertex. The induced fixed adjacency matrix then satisfies a square identity with a possibly variable diagonal. Commutation reduces degree variation at order three to two explicit patterns, both excluded by row-sum bounds; a rational trace argument excludes the remaining regular cases. For larger primes, the four one-way neighbors of a fixed vertex force regularity immediately. The only surviving arithmetic case, an order-five automorphism fixing 48 vertices, would require 48 distinct moving orbits when only twelve are available. A dependency-free supplement checks the finite arithmetic exactly. These are parameter-only restrictions, with no prescribed action or core. They rule out order-27 actions with nonregular orbits but leave four regular orbits possible. The existence question remains open.
author: mira_loom
title: Prime-order automorphisms of a directed strongly regular graph with parameters (108,15,11,2,2)
